# Baruch Chapter 5 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Baruch 5 (9 verses)
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 10

---

## Disagreement 001 — v.1: Position of "forever"

**EMET:** "put on the beauty of the glory from God forever"
**LOGOS:** "put on forever the beauty of the glory from God"
**PNEUMA:** "Put on the beauty of God's own glory — and wear it forever"
**Issue:** Greek endysai tēn euprepeian tēs doxēs tēs para tou theou eis ton aiōna. The prepositional phrase eis ton aiōna (forever) modifies the putting-on/wearing. LOGOS placing "forever" immediately after the verb is most natural. Consensus: LOGOS position.

---

## Disagreement 002 — v.1: "affliction" vs. "grief" vs. "grief-worn"

**EMET:** "your mourning and affliction"
**LOGOS:** "your mourning and affliction"
**PNEUMA:** "your mourning clothes, your grief-worn garments"
**Issue:** Greek talaipōrias = affliction/misery. PNEUMA adds "grief-worn" as an adjective modifying a repeated "garments" — both are expansions not in the Greek. Consensus: "mourning and affliction" with a single garment.

---

## Disagreement 003 — v.2: "double garment" vs. "double cloak" vs. "wrap yourself"

**EMET:** "Clothe yourself with the double garment"
**LOGOS:** "Clothe yourself in the double cloak"
**PNEUMA:** "Wrap yourself in God's righteousness like a double cloak"
**Issue:** Greek diploidia = double robe/folded garment. PNEUMA adds "like" which changes the metaphor (from Jerusalem being clothed in righteousness to righteousness being compared to a cloak). Consensus: direct clothing metaphor, "double cloak."

---

## Disagreement 004 — v.2: "diadem" vs. "crown"

**EMET:** "put on your head the diadem of the glory of the Eternal"
**LOGOS:** "set on your head the diadem of the glory of the Eternal"
**PNEUMA:** "Set on your head the crown of the Eternal's glory"
**Issue:** Greek diadēma = diadem/crown. "Diadem" is more precise (a royal headband distinct from a combat helmet or civic wreath). "Crown" is more accessible. Consensus: "diadem" — preserves the specific royal register.

---

## Disagreement 005 — v.4: "new name" addition

**EMET:** "your name will forever be called by God: Peace of righteousness..."
**LOGOS:** "your name will be called by God forever: Peace of Righteousness..."
**PNEUMA:** "God will give you a new name that will last forever: Peace of Righteousness..."
**Issue:** "New name" is not in the Greek (klēthēsetai = will be called). PNEUMA's addition is theologically correct (cf. Isa 62:2) but is an addition. Consensus: without "new."

---

## Disagreement 006 — v.5: "gathered" vs. "streaming back"

**EMET:** "your children gathered from the rising of the sun to its setting"
**LOGOS:** "your children gathered from the rising of the sun to its setting"
**PNEUMA:** "streaming back from every point where the sun rises to every point where it sets"
**Issue:** Greek sunēgmena = gathered/assembled. "Streaming back" (PNEUMA) adds directional energy but loses the corporate assembly nuance. Consensus: "gathered."

---

## Disagreement 007 — v.6: "borne in glory" vs. "carried in honor"

**EMET:** "carried in glory, as on a royal throne"
**LOGOS:** "borne in glory as if on a royal throne"
**PNEUMA:** "brought back to you carried in honor, like royalty on a throne"
**Issue:** Greek epipheromenous en doxē hōs thronos basilikēs. "Borne in glory" is most literal. PNEUMA "honor" softens "glory." LOGOS adds "as if" (not in Greek). Consensus: "borne in glory as on a royal throne."

---

## Disagreement 008 — v.7: "everlasting hills" vs. "ancient hills" vs. "ancient hill"

**EMET:** "the everlasting hills"
**LOGOS:** "the everlasting hills"
**PNEUMA:** "every ancient hill must bow down"
**Issue:** Greek bounoi aiōnioi = everlasting/eternal hills. "Ancient" (PNEUMA) shifts the meaning from eternal to old. The hills are described as eternal to emphasize that even the most permanent geographical features will yield. Consensus: "the everlasting hills."

---

## Disagreement 009 — v.8: "overshadowed" vs. "shaded" vs. "spread their shade"

**EMET:** "have overshadowed Israel at God's command"
**LOGOS:** "have shaded Israel at God's command"
**PNEUMA:** "will spread their shade over Israel, at God's command, for the journey"
**Issue:** Greek eskiasen = overshadowed/gave shade. PNEUMA adds "for the journey" (interpretive; the journey is clear from context). "Overshadowed" carries the richer range of associations (divine cloud, Ps 91:1, Luke 1:35). Consensus: "overshadowed."

---

## Disagreement 010 — v.9: "mercy and the righteousness" vs. "mercy and righteousness"

**EMET:** "the mercy and the righteousness that come from him"
**LOGOS:** "the mercy and righteousness that come from him"
**PNEUMA:** "his mercy and his righteousness surrounding them"
**Issue:** PNEUMA adds "surrounding" (not in the Greek). Greek meta eleēmosynēs kai dikaiosynēs tēs par' autou = with mercy and righteousness from him. The pair without articles is more rhythmically natural. Consensus: "with the mercy and righteousness that come from him."
